findings.source_passage: they will swear in the trance of the calm, and in the teeth of the tempest; they will imprecate curses from the topsail-yard-arms, when most they teeter over to a seething sea
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'To sailors, oaths are household words'
findings.why_it_matters: This rhythmic tricolon is the narrator's signature voice-establishing digression; it builds the rhetorical contrast that makes 'God's burning finger' land with force. The draft strips it to bare assertion, erasing the narrator's characteristic amplifying cadence.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full elaboration: 'they will swear in the trance of the calm, and in the teeth of the tempest; they will imprecate curses from the topsail-yard-arms, when most they teeter over to a seething sea; but in all my voyagings…'

findings.source_passage: do they only have mercy on long faces?—have they no bowels for a laugh?
findings.source_locator: Stubb's speech after Starbuck asks 'What thinkest thou now, man'
findings.why_it_matters: This is Stubb's defining comic-defiant voice in the face of the supernatural — the dark humor that characterizes him throughout. Its erasure flattens his character arc within the scene and removes the tonal counterpoint to the sublime before he pivots to the candles-as-sperm omen.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Stubb's opening lines: 'No, no, it wasn't; I said the corpusants have mercy on us all; and I hope they will, still. But do they only have mercy on long faces?—have they no bowels for a laugh?' before his sperm-oil speech.

summary: The draft preserves the critical signatures faithfully—Ahab's fire-soliloquy verbatim, the corpusants tableau, the harpoon-as-serpent, and the closing oath-extinguishing scene—but flattens the narrator's sailors-and-oaths cadence and drops Stubb's characteristic 'no bowels for a laugh' line, producing two medium-level voice losses that do not individually rise to regeneration.
